text:
sanjay: Quick heads-up — Snyk flagged a libssl chain CVE that requires rebuilding our minimal base image and rotating the cosign/KMS signing key. We should coordinate RBAC changes, audit logging, and the canary window.

emma: +1. timeline? can we do a staged push (staging -> canary -> prod) with audit hooks? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

lina: Prefer weekend low-traffic window. Need confirmation on who owns KMS rotate and who will update registry write perms. Also depends on whether we rebase or just patch.

ben: I can own the registry side and the canary rollout. Will need a short-lived service account for the build pipeline with ephemeral creds. Who will create it?

sanjay: Sec team creates the service account; we'll grant it the minimal roles: storage.objects.create + storage.objects.get for the staging bucket, and roles/registry.uploader for the canary namespace. After push, we remove the role.

emma: For KMS: plan is to rotate cosign signing key in KMS (key ring = projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/rebuild-2026). We should do a cold-start validation: sign one canary image and verify in CI. Also publish audit records to BigQuery.

lina: Audit logging — make sure to enable requestMetadata and principalSubject in the KMS logs so we can trace who performed the key operation. Also add a short retention tag and export to the audit-log project.

ben: For build creds, can we use ephemeral Workload Identity? Example command for cosign signing with KMS:

```bash
COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=1 
cosign sign --kms gcpkms://projects/redwood/locations/us/keyRings/rebuild-2026/cryptoKeys/cosign-key 
 gcr.io/redwood-staging/base:minimal-20260321
```

emma: yep — ensure the builder pod mounts the short-lived token and we call the KMS sign API using that identity. Sec-bot: please verify the policy for key access.

sec-bot: Automated check: existing IAM binding detected: roles/cloudkms.signerVerifier -> group:infra-builders@redwood.com. Proposed change: remove broad group binding and add per-service account binding for build-sa@infra.redwood.com.

sanjay: That aligns with least-privilege. Add a preflight doc outlining: 1) service account creation 2) IAM grant 3) one-time sign test 4) push canary 5) monitor audit logs for anomalous sign attempts.

lina: Vulnerability triage note: double-check transitive deps in the image (openssl-dev etc.). If we rebase, update the pinned package lists and run deterministic rebuilds. Add SBOM snapshot to the release artifact.

ben: Canary plan: push to gcr.io/redwood-canary/, hit two small k8s test clusters for 24h. If error rate <0.5% and no signing mismatches, promote to prod. I'll handle automated rollback scripts.

emma: For RBAC changes, timeline: Tue 02:00–05:00 UTC for preflight and staging push, Wed 01:00–04:00 UTC for canary -> prod. Does that work for infra oncall?

sanjay: Oncall ok. I'll schedule a short war-room channel and call the deploy bot to lock the gateway during the window. Also add a postmortem template if anything goes wrong.

lina: One more: update COSIGN public key thumbprint in trust store after rotate and create a mapping in the console UI so customers can verify provenance.

sec-bot: Checklist generated: [service-account, iam-bindings, kms-rotate, sign-test, sbom, canary-push, audit-export]. Please ack when complete.

ben: Ack from my side for registry/canary tasks.

emma: Ack for KMS/signing and audit exports.

sanjay: I'll create the service account and open PR for the IAM change. Adding the war-room thread at #release-war-room now.

lina: I'll run the image diffs and SBOMs and attach to the PR.

sec-bot: Action items locked. If anything blocks, ping @sanjay and add notes to the PR. Good luck. :rocket:
